storyText:
Mina woke up early in her small bedroom. The moon was white at the window, and rain made the roof wet. Her baby sister slept in a little bed with a yellow pillow. A cat sat at the door, a dog had a blue ball, and a bird ate bread from a red cup. Mina put apples, eggs, milk, cake, and ice in a black bag. Her father read a city letter at the kitchen table. "Maple House will close down in a week," the letter read. Mina talked her father round, and he agreed to help. She was glad to see Leo around the park as she left the house. Leo and Mina got about the city on a bus. At Maple House, Mina turned to her family for help. Her father dropped Mina and Leo off in his old car. "The class will finish up in the street," the letter read. Mina did not like that.

Leo wrote on the board, "A bad name on the city letter will trip up the plan." He asked the class to camp out in the garden and help with the bags at night. The bus had to slow down at the busy park road. Mina went to spy out a good room for the class. She and Leo sat at a round table to think the letter over. Mina went to see about money for the house. The long trip did Mina and Leo in. A name was missing. Mina wrote it in. Sara, her aunt, planned to go into science. She had a job at the hospital and carried a doctor bag and a map. A boy held a pen, and a girl held a flower. Their parent gave the children a picture of Maple House. In the picture, a king in a tall hat ate fish from a plate. A shoe sat at the door.

Grandmother believed in God. She asked the family to help. "We will help," Mina wrote. The Maple House plan was on the board. The ticket price for the family day had to go down. In a ball game at the park, Joon came on for a tired boy. Gray began to run Joon down for a bad kick. "Come off it, Gray," Mina cried. The long game wore Joon out, but his strong arm helped the class. Mina went over the game rule with Gray. Mina and Joon got on, and Gray became calm. At night, the baby turned over in her bed and put a hand on the pillow. Mina drank orange juice and read the letter. Her brother ate a banana, and her sister had warm milk. There was little money, but the family had a new plan.

Sara had to call in a doctor for the baby. A wet bathroom floor caught Leo out, but he did not fall. He dug a garden key out with a spoon. Mina chose a blue coat to go with her red hat. A closed door kept the children from the kitchen. Leo keyed in the family names on a computer. "Look out," Mina cried as a big ball came from the park. The class planned to make over the old room with clean white paint. Joon chose to play along with Gray as Gray acted like a famous captain. Mina played around with the camera picture. Blue was bad; red was good. She chose red and made a funny family picture. The picture made the baby happy, and her laugh filled the room.

Gray planned to put the letter over on the class as a city letter, but Mina found his name on it. Joon planned to run for class captain. The class ran into a difficult week with little money. Mina asked the family to give their gifts. At night, Mina saw the guests out at the center door. Joon ate a full cake. He went to sleep off the bad feeling from the heavy meal. The children stayed back from a small fire as Daddy cooked dinner. Grandmother stored up bread, milk, sugar, salt, and water for the new day. Grandfather put a warm blanket on the bed. Mina put the blue bag on a table and closed the door. She knew the house was old, but it was beautiful. Her family liked the quiet room, the bright clock, and the picture on the wall. Mina went to sleep with the city letter in her hand.

In the morning, the family made breakfast in the kitchen. Mina cut bread, her mother cooked eggs, and her father made coffee. The baby had a cup of milk, and the young boy had orange juice. "My bag is on this table, and your bag is there," Mina wrote for Leo. "This black bag is my bag, and that blue bag is his. They ask us for help, and our family will help their family. I will carry the letter, and you will carry the money," Mina wrote. A good name came to Mina: Maple House. The family left the apartment as the city day began. A bus came from the street, and Mina gave Daddy the address. Daddy knew the way to the center. Mina looked at Leo, and they began their long day.


Grandmother took to a fast morning walk, and Grandfather walked with her. The new camera came with a bag. Mina wrote back to her aunt at the country farm. The family set to and made the center clean. At lunch, they ordered in bread, fruit, juice, and a hot meal. The job went on as the children ate. Joon took up guitar and began to practice. A plan came to Mina as she read the letter from her aunt. Daddy put in a computer at the class door. Mina put on a clean white jacket. Her brother put a soft blanket on a little bed. The class had a big job, but the children were ready.

Dark rain set in, but the family set out for the farm. They went for the old blue truck, not the new red car. Mina read a lesson, but it did not go in as the bus was loud and crowded. A fire bell went off at the city hospital. Black coats went out that winter, but Sara liked her old coat. Mina went through a box of clothes for the family day. A high window was hard to get at. They got back to the bus with a heavy bag. The sky was cloudy, the air was cold, and the road was wet. Mina felt tired, but Leo was excited to see the farm.

The family got in at the farm at night, and Daddy got off the job at that hour. A nurse got the dog out of the bathroom. Mina got over a cold with sleep and warm bread. She got through a long letter from her father. The children made for the garden, and a cow came to meet Mina and Leo. Mina made little of the old farm map. Leo made out a small island in the lake. Grandfather took over the camera job and asked the children to be at the bridge. A funny picture came about as Leo walked fast. A happy calm came over Mina as she saw her family.

A phone call came through from Maple House. The family day was coming up, and the farm had gifts to give. Grandmother looked after a cow, a sheep, and a young animal. She looked back on a happy day in her garden at the beach. A boy and a girl looked on as Daddy fixed a bicycle. Mina looked up the boat time on the computer. The rain was strong, but her father did not give in. He did not back down from the trip. Cars began to back up on the mountain road. The family sat in the truck and listened to the radio. A bright light from a church tower helped Daddy find the road.

Mina and Leo worked out a short way to the center. They did not put off the trip. They kept on as rain covered the road. In the slow truck, they kept up. At the farm house, a candle made the dark kitchen bright. The family ate fresh fruit, butter, bread, and a potato meal. Mina drank cold water, and her brother had a sandwich. Her aunt gave the baby a cute toy rabbit. The cow had a white body, black hair, a long leg, and a strong foot. A turtle lived at the garden pool. Joon played guitar as the family talked. Sara read a newspaper page and helped Grandfather with his knee. The children walked to the field and the boat and sat at the lake. They slept in a comfortable room and got ready for the morning truck.

The farm was at a deep forest and a high mountain. A river crossed the field and went to the ocean. A small island was in the lake, and a boat was at the beach. Grandfather grew tomato plants, potatoes, and fresh vegetables. Grandmother fed the cow, the sheep, a bird, and a little turtle. Mina collected eggs in a basket, and Leo carried fruit in a box. Daddy fixed the truck engine and checked the map. Sara taught air, fire, earth, and water in a science lesson. The children listened and learned from her. At dinner, the family had a full plate and a cold drink. The beds were warm in the quiet night. "The farm gift will help Maple House," Mina wrote.


The old bus was slow, and Mina had to run fast. The market was full. Gray had to turn a car away. Mina turned on her phone at the bakery. Leo turned up with a brown basket and a bottle of orange juice. They went to the city office to hand in the center letter. Wet blue paint showed up on the paper. A small child did not like the market and ran away with Mina's bag. His mother caught the child. Mina ran through the plan in a calm way. The meal price ran to their full bag of money. Mina and Leo finished that job and chose to move on to the bank job.

The market office planned to move out of the old apartment at the river. Mina held in a cry. A strong arm held up a bright bell in the round tower, and a deep bridge crossed the river. Leo brought up the family day and the blue paint. A woman asked Mina to write in her address. She booked the boat captain in at a cheap hotel. Mina and Leo took a bad road and ended up at the museum. A golden balloon at the door made the museum stand out. The artist cut down the price of a beautiful painting. Joon cut in as Mina began to pay.

The phone line cut Joon off, but Mina carried on. Daddy's truck broke down on the mountain road. Light broke through the cloudy sky and made the river bright. Mina picked out a clean box for the camera. Leo met her at the library to catch up. They ruled out the airport, the island, and the beach. Night began to close in at the old castle. A bank rule went against their plan, and the bank did not lend Mina and Leo money. Mina was angry, but Leo helped her become calm. They chose a short road to the center.

Mina and Leo went around the museum with a quiet guest. Butter and warm bread go together, but the children had to go without lunch. Mina got the hotel address down on a newspaper page. The family planned to get together at the center. Leo had to take a heavy camera back to the store. The students took down the high birthday wall at the center. Sara asked Mina to come along to the bakery. The artist gave out a map, a calendar, and a picture. The captain did not back out of the river trip. Mina called out as the wet basket fell. A friendly woman opened the museum and let Mina and Leo in.

The woman let Mina into a family plan for the old camera. Mina turned down a free hotel room and chose the center. The museum held a glass box, a soft bench, and a bright painting. A girl listened as the artist taught her to paint a rainbow. A boy opened a box and found a round orange. The captain carried a map and drove a toy car in a game. Mina began to dance, and Joon began to sing with his guitar. A toy plane flew in a blue ocean picture. Mina heard the bell and called Daddy. Leo bought bread, butter, and a cold drink for lunch. The cook cut fruit and made a delicious meal. The children left with a picture, a gift, and a better plan for the fair.

The market had a bakery, a bank, a bookstore, a restaurant, and a clothes shop. A hotel was at a street corner, and a church was at the town center. A visitor from a village bought a newspaper and a bottle of water. A pilot from the airport ate lunch with a boat captain. A college artist gave a castle painting for money. A factory guest carried a camera and a radio. Mina saw prices on the gifts and counted her money. The blue bag was not at the store, the office, or the museum. She felt sad, but Leo asked her to continue. They had a chance to help the center, and the missing bag did not end their plan.


At Maple House, the students started on the fair map at a circle of desks. Grandmother handed down her old warm coat to her young daughter. Bored children began to play up on the clean floor. Rain ran off the roof and crossed the ground. Leo held out a dry shirt for Mina. The dinner lesson was held over for a full hour. The office woman did not water down the important letter. Mina did not write off the center as a lost house. Daddy asked the family to sit back for a minute, and a tired guest sat the ball game out. The room was noisy, but the plan was clear.

Their hard job began to pay off as the center became clean. A nervous girl began to grow into a brave captain. The church dance began to grow on Joon. Mina walked into a glass door and had a bad knee. A college student began to wait on the hungry guests. The bakery sold out of cookies and fresh cake. The class planned to carry the fair through. Daddy got in the truck and drove off to the factory. A happy guest broke into a dance as Joon played guitar. A tree fell, and a small arm of the tree broke off. The rain became heavy, and the family closed the window.

Gray began to pick on a small child, and Mina asked Gray to be kind. Sara phoned in from the hospital. A baby was at the center for help. Gray caught on and gave the child a friendly hand. Mina stepped out to check the dangerous road. She drew in cool air at the forest door. Sara drew out the quiet girl with a good language game. The girl threw off her wet coat and gave it to her mother. Heavy rain threw up a broken door at the center. Visitors had to sign in at the desk. Mina signed off her city letter with a little flower. Gray did not answer back as Mina gave Gray a helpful job.

"The children will not miss out on the holiday dinner," Mina wrote on the board. She fished a key out of her deep pocket. The class began to wind down with hot coffee and cookies. Leo wound up the lesson with a clever plan for the fair. The family had to ride out the dark night at the church. Daddy sat at the old engine. Mina and Sara shopped around for a cheap knife, glass cups, and a new plate. Joon cried out as a turtle came alive at his foot. The children blew up a golden balloon and a blue balloon. They dressed up as a captain, a doctor, a pilot, and a famous king. The students cleaned out the party room and found a huge mirror. Wet paint had to dry out. They opened the window.

The rain continued, and the class did not leave. Daddy arrived with farm gifts in the truck. Mina borrowed a plate, and Leo lent her a cup. They collected bread and counted cookies. A parent covered the floor and filled a box with fresh fruit. Sara fixed Joon's knee and fed the little turtle. The family followed a line to dinner. Mina did not forget the center or lose her dream. Mina found the hard night interesting. The earth was wet, but a rainbow filled the sky as morning began. Mina was hungry and thirsty, but she felt alive. Gray gave her a healthy vegetable sandwich. His kind act made Mina glad.

The center had a basement, a bedroom, a bathroom, a kitchen, and a full party room. A high ceiling covered the room, and a new carpet covered the floor. A mirror was at the wall with a candle. A piano, a guitar, a radio, and a computer were ready. A desk held paper, pencils, a notebook, and a calendar. A coat, a shirt, socks, and shoes were dry at the fire. A bottle, a bowl, a plate, a knife, and a spoon were at the breakfast table. A flower, a plant, and a seed sat at the window. The bad weather was difficult, but the family was helpful. Their job made the old center feel new.


Water in the little garden pool began to dry up. The church planned to ring in the new year at the fair. Sara gave Joon time for his knee care to kick in. A bad guest planned to enter a closed room. Daddy had to kick the guest out. Mina washed the cake out of her white shirt with soap. Her mother washed up the plates, cups, bowls, and spoons. Leo penciled in piano practice for a full hour. A student had to do a party picture over on fresh paper. Mina did not take against Gray. She knew a hard day made a good woman angry.

Joon took apart the old radio for the science table. The family went to the station to see a pilot off. Mina asked Joon to man up and carry the heavy box with her. The cook kept back salt, sugar, cheese, and potatoes for dinner. Leo brought the fixed radio round to Mina's house. The boat captain had to push off from the sea wall. Mina checked the finished jobs off in her notebook. Sara asked the class to sing out at the piano. A tired child slept through the radio call. A cute rabbit had holed up in a box at the shop. Mina gave the rabbit a vegetable and called the farm.

The store planned to ship out a box of toys for the fair. The restaurant farmed out the bread job to the bakery. The family sat at the center for the rain to blow over. The college students dressed down in clean shirts and socks. Daddy had to bear down on a hard engine button. The cook dished out a fresh potato meal. Mina did not brush aside the broken roof. Leo had on a blue shirt with a golden star. The family had their neighbor round for a movie. A red line in the blue bag had to do with the missing fair prize. Mina began to believe that the bag came from the bookstore.

The class asked Mina to go ahead with the fair. The families got behind her plan. Joon got onto a city radio game and talked of Maple House. He had to get up early and practice. The class made a boring room into a comfortable movie room. Mina thought back to the blue bag at breakfast. She came away from the market with a new guess. Leo came back from the store with a present and a bookstore letter. The plan came before the city board, and the board agreed. Heavy rain came down on the crowded street. Officer Kim came for the bag, as Gray's name was on it. Mina asked Officer Kim to sit and read the letter.

The honest bookstore woman came forward with Rose's blue bag. The bags came from her bookstore. She had given a bag to Gray and a bag to Rose, but the names disappeared in rain. The woman was rich, and her clothes were clean. She carried a ticket, a candy box, and a letter with her address. Her shop was at the corner with a flat roof. Mina asked her to discuss the bags with Gray. They opened the bags and discovered the name change. Gray was not a bad boy, and Mina was not afraid of Gray. Officer Kim was happy and left in the city car. The sunny sky made the wet street bright. The fair went on, and the children began to laugh.

The woman gave Maple House a prize for the fair. The expensive camera came from her shop. Gray folded the blue bags and put the bags in a basket. Mina fixed a broken chain at the center door. Joon painted a rainbow on a board. Sara baked bread and added cheese to the lunch table. Daddy built a bench, and Grandfather balanced it on the flat ground. Grandmother made the carpet clean and put a blanket on the piano. The children practiced a dance, and Joon practiced guitar. A lazy cat slept at the fire as a dog began to bark. The busy room felt normal. Mina enjoyed the fair and was not afraid.


At fair morning, Rose came in with her blue bag. Mina came upon a zoo ticket and a small picture in the pocket. The ticket came with a map of the city. Leo wanted in on it. They looked around the bookstore, looked at the names, and looked for Rose at the park. In a ball game, Joon gave the game away with a bad kick. He gave the ball back to a little boy. Mina worked in a blue bag line as she practiced her fair talk. Sara worked on the bookstore woman, and the woman agreed to help the center.

The office called Mina back at breakfast. Parents called for the city to leave Maple House open at lunch. The fair began. Rain came, but the class did not call off the fair. The captain called on the town to help. Mina had left her black bag behind in the truck. She put a full week into the fair. Leo put a plan to the family at the board. They put together a wall of family pictures. A chain kept the dog away from the vegetable bowl. Mina kept Gray in for a minute, and Sara asked Joon to keep off cake. The rain let up, and bright weather brought the town to Maple House.

Mina and Sara talked the plan over at the window. The newspaper talked up the fair as a great town day. The class turned around the lunch job in a full hour. Mina did not turn Gray in, as Gray had not taken the bag. In a cartoon, a golden toy queen turned into a cat. Daddy turned off the radio as the city chose. The blue bag turned out to be Rose's bag. Mina wrote, "Class will start back in autumn, and Rose will have a new job at Maple House." Students handed out a map and showed Rose around the center. Rose had heard about Maple House from her uncle, but she had not heard of Mina.

Little children played at being a pilot, a doctor, a young artist, and a king. Parents ran around with cake, cheese, tomato sandwiches, and hot water. Sara had a chance to move up to a better city job, but she chose Maple House. Mina lived for days like this. Grandmother planned to live out her years at the park road. The fair was excellent, and the center did not disappear. Children had a chance to learn, exercise, act, bake, and celebrate. The noisy room became calm as night came. The winter air was cold, but the fire burned warm. Mina greeted visitors at the door and was happy. Rose felt lonely and nervous, but she joined the class. Mina invited a polite passenger from the station. Families gathered from the town area and a city block. Joon lifted a box, and Leo pulled a table. The children beat the difficult day with a game that was easy.

In a new week, Mina sat on a bench at a high tree. Her favorite coat was warm, and a new button held it closed. A brush was in her bag, and a toy truck was in Leo's bag. Joon bit his apple and checked his tooth and mouth in a mirror. Rose delivered paper from the bookstore and put it on a board. A visitor brought a carpet, a cartoon picture, and a bottle for the basement. A visitor in a blue uniform brought a train toy from a vacation. The center bedroom had a perfect ceiling and a small window. Mina asked guests to write names and ages. She planned to discover a new language game and discuss it with Sara. The blue bags belonged at Maple House, and Maple House was in the town. The family fair changed Maple House. Mina knew the change had happened: a city had become a family. Students finished their homework at the empty desk, and Rose made a dirty board clean. Mina explained the bag change to the class. "Maple House will depend on family help," she wrote.

A new season came, and the garden grew rich with flowers. Sunny weather brought a holiday and a trip to the lake. In autumn, the class collected golden leaves. In winter, children made a warm camp at the center. A pilot talked of a plane, a captain talked of a boat, and Grandfather talked of the earth. The artist painted the ocean, a nurse taught healthy care, and a cook baked delicious bread. A student read a newspaper, wrote a letter, and copied a map. A girl climbed a tree, a boy kicked a ball, and children swam in the lake. A baby laughed with a cute toy, and a grandmother sang at the piano. Maple House was free, friendly, fair, and full. Mina looked at the blue bags on the wall. They were little bags, but they carried a great family dream to the world.
